area: clAInk.io (id: claink): the advertisement, the two-step purchase with its policy step, the agent workspace, the two minimized bars, and what a player can learn of the financial terms before buying. Scratch work is in test-results/audit/claink/.
summary: clAInk's look, numbers and layouts hold up: the price line, the $500 button and the fine print survive every ad layout at every size checked, the workspace's arithmetic matches the rules, and nothing overflows on a phone. Two things are worth fixing: nothing a player can read states what a run costs until the first bill (a $0 run bills $529 to $1,649, median $980), and on laptop-height windows the strike card, "Closed: $0" and the Friday estimate land out of sight when Run agents is pressed; four smaller disclosure points and one nit follow.
verified_ok: Coverage: 137 static states (ad, policy step, dismissal question, minimized ad, ten-deal board, week 3, insufficient cash, seven workspace states, minimized workspace, cancel question, freeze, two-strike variants) at 1920x1080, 1440x900, 1366x768, 1280x720, 390x844 touch and 320x568 touch, plus spot checks at 768x1024 and 1024x768; 42 scripted runs in the test build and 9 real presses of Run agents in release.html. No page errors and no horizontal overflow in any of them. About 45 pictures were opened and read; the rest were judged from measurements (in sight, hidden, overflowing).

Terms a player can read before buying, stated plainly: the upfront price ($500 on 'Begin your transformation', on 'Accept', in the handbook); that usage is billed on Fridays and idle weeks bill too (fine print, handbook); what a strike is (policy step line 2, handbook); that strike 3 revokes the seat (policy step, handbook); the one-in-five success rate and that the other four runs bill outcomes anyway (fine print; handbook '20%'); the week 3 deadline (badge, minimized bar, fine print, handbook); the $250 cancellation fee (handbook only). Absent or understated terms are findings 1, 4 and 5.

The ad's financial terms survive every layout. Across all 32 desktop ad states the price line, the $500 button and the fine print are present and in sight, and the open ad never scrolls inside itself. Only the announcement, feature chips, badges and testimonial leave (1280x720 with ten deals: 'tight announce chips badges proof', 355 px, all three terms in sight; same with the dismissal question open). When the badges leave, the deadline is still in the fine print.

Phones: the ad starts as a one-line bar directly under End week ('clAInk · Pilot pricing ends week 3', 44 px expand and dismiss buttons); expanded it is complete at 390 and 320 wide with nothing left out; the policy step shows its three lines with 'Accept · $500' and 'Not now' in view; the workspace reads cleanly, cancel question included (shots/x-ws-cancel-ask@320x568.clip.png).

Numbers agree between ad, bars, workspace, handbook, log and rules: $500 (button, Accept, log '−$500', 'Charged back so far $500', handbook); 1 in 5 and 20% (20.1% of 20,000 simulated first runs); week 3; three strikes; true-up −$200 to −$1,800 with Collections at −$1,500 (two-strike note and handbook); $250 cancel fee (handbook and question); idle $150 to $300 (simulated idle invoices 150 to 300, up to 895 with an overage).

Workspace arithmetic: 'Estimated this week: $669' is what Friday's log line charges ('clAInk invoice: 2.7M tokens, 2 outcomes. −$669'); the cancel question's $919 is $250 plus that $669; the revoked card's 'Charged back $7,000' is $669 plus the $6,331 true-up; the two-strike note is right in each variant tried (cash $300: '−$229 to −$1,800'; cash −$1,000: 'sends you to Collections'; after this week's run: 'worse if you're in the red').

Billable outcomes are distinct from revenue wherever both show: a purple 'Run n · Outcomes delivered' box ending in pink 'Closed: $0' against a green 'Revenue verified' box ending 'Closed +$17,000 · verified by Finance'; log '5 billable outcomes, 4.9M tokens, $0 closed' against '2 signed, $17,000 closed. Commission: $2,040'; revoked recap 'Claimed influence $80,000 · Closed $0 · Charged back $7,000'.

Strike cards and incident reports are readable when in sight: each of the four incidents prints what it took ('Feral Unicorn walked · −10 reputation · −6 manager', 'ByteBazaar −45% · −10 manager · −4 reputation', 'Lost 2 deals, $27,000 · −12 reputation · −8 manager', '−$6,600 closed · −$792 commission clawed back'). All clAInk text is 13 px or larger; measured contrast against the painted backdrop is 10:1 to 16:1 on cards, 4.9 to 6.2:1 on the ad's fine print, 6.1:1 on 'Cancel seat'.
The two-strike warning sits directly under Run agents and is in sight at every size, 1280x720 and phones included.

The cancel control is quiet and works: a muted underlined link at the foot; its question scrolls into sight at every size; 'Insufficient cash to cancel safely' is disabled when paying would reach Collections; week 13 shows the freeze text and no cancel.

Minimized bars agree with what they stand for: 'clAInk · Pilot pricing ends week 3' ('ends this week' in week 3) with expand and a dismiss that asks first; 'clAInk Ready · 1/3 strikes' with expand. 37 px tall on a desktop, 55 px on a phone.

Purchase in release.html on desktop and phone: cash $1,200 to $700, log 'clAInk seat activated. The expense has been allocated to you. −$500', focus lands on the workspace's status line. The release page exposes no dice hook.

The contrast with Shitcorp is intact: gradients, pill buttons and glow appear only inside clAInk's surfaces, at every size. Seen and not raised: on stacked layouts the button band leaves a faint hard edge in the ad's corner glow (crop-cta-390.png).

findings.title: What a run costs is never stated before the first bill: not in the ad, the policy step, the handbook, or on the Run button
findings.where: src/copy/help.js:51 (handbook row); src/copy/clainkUi.js:27, 35, 41 (price line, policy, fine print), :92 (Run button note), :97 (usage line before a run); rules src/game/claink.js:43-47; facts src/game/selectors.js:120
findings.evidence: Rules: a week you run bills $249 plus $140 to $280 per outcome; a $0 run bills 2 to 5 outcomes, so $529 to $1,649. 20,000 first runs through src/game (sim.mjs): $0-run usage median $980, mean $987; Friday invoice including the 10% overage median $1,020, highest $2,072. None of the 1,928 strings in strings.json carries $249, $140 to $280 or the overage's $200 to $600. Before purchase a player can read: ad 'Outcome-based pricing. Pay for outcomes and the compute required to deliver them.'; fine print 'Usage is billed on Fridays, even while idle.'; policy step 'Seat and usage charges are deducted from your cash.'; handbook 'Pay $500 upfront, deploy once per eligible week with zero slots/energy, pay usage on Friday. ... Idle weeks still bill.' After purchase and before the first run (shots/bought@1280x720.png): 'Run agents · 0 energy · 0 slots · billed Friday', no hint or tooltip on the button, and the only weekly figure in sight is 'Idle weeks still bill $150–$300', about a quarter of what the button bills. The price first appears after the run ('Estimated this week: $1,299'). New game, buy, one press, End Week with nothing else spent: of 15,978 simulated $0 runs, 40.9% reach −$1,000 or lower and 2.7% are repossessed that first Friday. The build matches the copydeck word for word (lines 295, 362, 365, 387, 393) and 2.0.1's handbook did not state the price either, so the gap is in the approved sentences, not in their implementation.
findings.proposal: State the tariff where the rules are read, fed from the CLAINK constants so it cannot drift. handbookFacts gains retainer, perOutcome, outcomes and idle; the handbook row says 'pay usage on Friday: $249 a run plus $140–$280 per billed outcome (two to five on a $0 run)' and 'Idle weeks still bill $150–$300'. If the owner also wants it in sight at the button, put the same clause at the front of the pre-run usage line (CK_WORKSPACE.usageIdle). The ad itself can stay as vague as it is.
findings.risk: Both are approved copydeck sentences: each needs an 'owner' note in docs/2.1/copy-coverage-notes.json and new lint params. The handbook is 849 px of an 876 px limit at 1440x900, so two more lines may make it scroll there (it already scrolls at 1366x768 and 1280x720). A longer usage line pushes 'Cancel seat' one more line under the fold on short windows. Players who see the price may buy less often; no rule changes.

findings.title: On laptop-height windows, pressing Run agents lands the strike card, 'Closed: $0' and the Friday estimate out of sight, and the workspace does not follow
findings.where: src/ui/ClainkUi.jsx: the report's playback (lines 381-408) and finishReveal (366-372) never move the workspace's scroll; the cancel question does (345-348). Share of the column: src/styles/claink.css:216-218, fade at :242.
findings.evidence: 'The fold' is the bottom edge of the workspace's visible box; on a desktop it scrolls inside that box. Shipping file release.html, ck-active-0-strikes.json (week 2, four deals), press Run agents, three presses per size (release-run.cjs); scrollTop stayed 0 every time. 1280x720: strike card 0 px in sight (of 57 to 76), 'Closed: $0' 7 of 24 px, 'Estimated this week' 0 px, 'Cancel seat' 0 px; the last line in sight in live/release-run@1280x720-2.png is 'Marked HyperLobster Closed Won. Finance disagrees.' 1366x768: card 0 to 34 px of 57 to 76, estimate 0 px. 1440x900: all whole. Test build with scripted dice on the same board: at 1536x730 and 1440x790 (a 1080p or 900p screen inside a browser window) the card shows 0 px and 35 of 99 px. A churn strike at 1280x720 takes $6,600 of closed revenue and $792 of cash; the one line that says so is out of sight and the log says only 'Strike 1/3 (Customer Success): A customer upgraded to 3×, then churned.' (live/strike-hurt-churn@1280x720.png). Third strike at 1280x720: the true-up line shows 5 of 18 px and the REVOKED card 0 px. A position scrolled by hand survives End Week: next week Run agents and the strike boxes are scrolled out (scrollTop 152 at 1280x720, 86 at 1366x768; live/next-week-after-scroll@1280x720.png). No gate sees this: test/e2e/matrix.cjs:183 scrolls the card into view by script before checking it. On record already: a report taller than its room fades at the fold (CHANGELOG.md:42), and the release notes' 'on an early board a run's whole report shows, strike card and all' holds from 1440x900 up. The same file treats the same situation as a defect for the cancel question ('you pressed the link and saw no buttons').
findings.proposal: Extend the cancel question's rule to a run the player just pressed: when its card lands below the fold, move the workspace's own scroll (never the page's) so the card and the line under it are in sight, and set it back to the top when the week turns. A reload stays at the top as now. Nothing changes where the workspace does not scroll (1440x900 and up on an early board, and phones).
findings.risk: After a run on a short window the status line, the spent Run button and the strike boxes scroll out (the title bar is sticky and the card repeats 'Strike n of 3'). Programmatic focus sits on the status line (line 475), which would then be out of sight. With reduced motion it is a jump, not a glide. It needs its own layout check beside dock-question-seen, and matrix.cjs:183's scripted scroll would hide a regression.

findings.title: End week's Friday preview lists salary and rent but not the clAInk invoice
findings.where: src/copy/ui.js:103 (HINT.endWeek); src/game/selectors.js:58-61 (fridayPreview); the invoice itself is src/game/week.js:135
findings.evidence: release.html, ck-report-strike-hurt.json (the agents ran; the workspace says 'Estimated this week: $669 ... billed Friday'): hovering End week shows 'End week. Friday: salary +$1,000, energy +15, stress −4. Friday events and collections may change this.' (shots/endhint-ck-report-strike-hurt@1440x900.png). The same text shows with an idle seat that will bill $150 to $300 (ck-active-2-strikes.json). Rent is listed when due: 'salary +$1,000, rent −$1,600' (fresh.json). The invoice is as certain as rent: the amount already due when the agents ran, $150 to $300 when they did not. At 1366x768 and 1280x720 the workspace's own estimate is below the fold (finding 2), so this hint is the only Friday summary in sight and it leaves the bill out.
findings.proposal: fridayPreview gains the seat's charge: for an active seat outside the week 13 freeze, the amount due if the agents ran, otherwise the idle range. HINT.endWeek prints one clause after rent: ', clAInk −$669' or ', clAInk −$150–$300'.
findings.risk: This is the hint bar, which brief section 1 (action clarity) owns, so it may collide with that work. One more clause can take the hint to a third line at 1280 wide (it is two lines there today). src/ui/app/Kpis.jsx:45 reads the same selector and the facts tests pin its fields.

findings.title: The handbook no longer says a strike can do damage, and words the true-up less plainly than 2.0.1 did
findings.where: src/copy/help.js:51; 2.0.1's row for comparison: test/baseline/checkpoint-engine/src/copy/help.js:42; rule src/game/claink.js:34-40
findings.evidence: 2.1: 'every $0 run earns a strike. Idle weeks still bill. Third strike revokes the seat, may cost a live deal, and charges a true-up based on cash plus $200–$1,800.' 2.0.1: 'the rest burn tokens on billed "outcomes" and earn a strike, sometimes with damage. Strike 3: seat revoked, a deal walks, and a true-up takes all your cash plus $200–$1,800.' Rule: 38% of strikes 1 and 2 do real damage (37.9% of 15,978 simulated $0 runs): the most advanced deal walks, a 45% discount, two deals leaked, or 22% of closed revenue and its commission taken back. Nothing a player can read before the first incident says so: not the ad, the policy step ('Every run without closed revenue earns an AI Governance Council strike.'), the handbook, or the workspace note ('Every run that closes $0 is a strike. 3 and the seat is revoked.'). The README does ('Some strikes do real damage to your deals, your closed revenue, your reputation or your manager's patience'). The 2.1 sentence is the copydeck's, verbatim (line 295).
findings.proposal: Restore the two phrases inside the 2.1 sentence: 'every $0 run earns a strike, sometimes with real damage' and 'charges a true-up of all your cash plus $200–$1,800'.
findings.risk: An approved copydeck sentence, so it needs an 'owner' note. One more line in the handbook's longest row (see finding 1 on its height). The owner may prefer the first incident to stay a surprise; if so, leave the first phrase out and keep the second.

findings.title: 'A live deal may walk' at two strikes, but the rule always takes your most advanced deal
findings.evidence: The rule has no roll: 'const lost=[...s.deals].sort(ckRank)[0]||null; if(lost){ s.deals=s.deals.filter(d=>d.id!==lost.id) ...'. Four of four scripted third strikes on ck-active-2-strikes.json removed DataRamen, the $18,000 Proposal at the top of the list ('Its farewell email to DataRamen: "We've decided to pursue other opportunities." They agreed.', live/revoke@1440x900.png). The note under Run agents, whose job is to say what the next strike costs, reads 'Next $0 run is strike 3: seat revoked, a live deal may walk, and the token true-up leaves you around −$200 to −$1,800.' 2.0.1 said 'a deal walks'. The copydeck changed it only for an empty pipeline (line 368: 'Replace "a deal walks" with "a live deal may walk" if pipeline can be empty'), and the build applies 'may' whether or not there are deals.
findings.proposal: ClainkStrikes already receives the run's cash and what is due; pass it whether there are deals. With deals the note says 'your most advanced deal walks'; with none the clause is left out. The policy step and the handbook can keep 'may', since they speak before any pipeline exists.
findings.risk: A copydeck deviation (owner note). The note is already three lines at 1280 wide and on phones, so the wording must not add a fourth.

findings.title: At 1366x768 and 1280x720 'Cancel seat' and the usage line sit below the workspace's fold once any report is showing
findings.where: src/ui/ClainkUi.jsx:484-499 (the usage line and the cancel link are the workspace's last children); src/styles/claink.css:216-218
findings.evidence: Measured at load, nothing scrolled (measure.json). 1920x1080 and 1440x900: both in sight in all five active states. 1366x768: in sight only before the first run; after one, 'Cancel seat' starts 23 to 77 px below the fold and the usage line 21 to 50 px. 1280x720: 'Cancel seat' is never wholly in sight and starts 71 to 162 px below the fold with a report showing. At two strikes, where cancelling matters most, the red warning is in sight and the exit is 77 px (1366x768) or 162 px (1280x720) under last week's report (shots/ws-2@1280x720.png). It is reachable by scrolling the workspace, and its question does scroll into sight once pressed.
findings.proposal: If finding 2 is taken, the player sees the foot of the workspace after every run and this needs nothing more. Otherwise the smallest change is order: while the agents have not run this week, show the usage line and 'Cancel seat' before last week's report.
findings.risk: Reordering changes the idle workspace at every size, and the cancel question's rule (line 348) scrolls to the foot, so it would have to aim at the question instead. Leaving this alone is defensible.

findings.title: When the workspace scrolls it shows the browser's default 15 px scrollbar, the only unstyled one in the game
findings.where: src/styles/claink.css:99-100 (.claink-console has overflow:auto and no scrollbar rule); compare src/styles/app.css:124 (.scroll: thin, themed)
findings.evidence: Playwright hides scrollbars, so no QA picture or gate has shown this. With them shown (scrollbar.cjs, 1280x720, ck-report-strike-hurt.json) the workspace is 496 px wide with 481 px of content: a 15 px classic scrollbar with arrow buttons down the vendor's panel (shots/scrollbar-shown@1280x720.clip.png). The deal list and the log use 'scrollbar-width:thin; scrollbar-color:var(--border-strong) transparent'. Players on Windows and Linux see it at 1366x768 and below after every run; macOS overlay scrollbars do not show it.
findings.proposal: One rule in clAInk's own stylesheet: .claink-console{scrollbar-width:thin; scrollbar-color:var(--ck-line) transparent}.
findings.risk: The content gains about 7 px of width while the workspace scrolls, which can move a line break and so a measured height; the headless gates never see a scrollbar either way.

not_checked: Only Chromium was available: no Firefox or Safari, where sticky positioning, dvh units and scrollbar styling can differ.

No real devices: touch scrolling of the workspace inside its dock, on-screen keyboards and safe-area insets were not exercised. Finding 7's scrollbar was seen in Linux headless Chromium only, not on Windows or macOS.

Screen-reader output: the live region and labels were read in the code, not heard. Keyboard-only use of the ad and workspace was read in the code (focus targets, Esc), with only the focus after purchase observed.
Reduced motion: no run was played with it on; the code shows the whole report at once.
The manager taking a deal (the Writing Lesson dialog) was not played; only his first warning was.
Landscape phones and windows 600 px tall or less (where the bars are the default) were not pictured. Tablets got two spot checks only (768x1024, 1024x768).
Boards larger than ten deals beside the ad, and the workspace beside 24 deals in live play, were not re-measured; the QA report's own table covers them.
Balance was not evaluated, as instructed. The simulation in sim.mjs measures what a first week costs under the existing rules and proposes no change to any price or probability.
The ending screens' clAInk lines and distinctions, beyond the revoked and cancelled cards in the workspace.
Old saves: the fixtures carry 2.0.1's stored report wording by design; it was not judged. Real 2.1 report text was checked through scripted runs instead.
On a phone the announcer's caption covers part of the strike card for as long as the caption shows (live/strike-hurt-slop@390x844.png); it is transient and belongs to captions, so it was not pursued.
The 2.1.1 working copy: all evidence is from the frozen 2.1 builds and from src at HEAD. If brief section 1 has already changed the End week hint, finding 3 needs re-checking against that text.
